status: 12 drafts for independent review, not accepted or runtime
reviewNote: Every exact URL was opened and reviewed. Twelve distinct Commons original SHA1 values. Ten bindings reuse unaccepted draft01 photographs with new prose, plus two fresh sources. No accepted draft01 SHA1 is reused. Remembered events are fiction; per-entry scene limitations are explicit. Entries 03, 07, 08, 11 and 12 need especially strict prose review; count is not a quality endorsement.

entries.subject: river
entries.title: A demonstration
entries.body:
He explained that the stone needed to be flat. Then he explained the wrist. His daughter waited with a round stone in each hand.

He crouched, chose a better stone, changed it for another, and asked her to watch carefully.

One magnificent plop.

She laughed so hard she dropped both her stones. Two smaller plops. This made it worse.

He stood there with his throwing arm still out. Then he started laughing too.

They spent the next hour throwing increasingly unsuitable stones into me. By the end she needed both hands to lift hers.

image.sceneMatch: Pebble beach with one seated person beside the Soča at Deskle. Stones, visitors and river are visible. The father and daughter and their throws are invented remembered events, not visible in the photo. Pairing needs lead review because only one person is pictured.

entries.subject: river
entries.title: A good listener
entries.body: A woman sat beside me crying. I nearly asked what had happened, but she was already surrounded by the sound of someone who couldn't stop talking.

image.sceneMatch: Clear water alongside a low limestone edge supports a place to sit and the river's close physical presence. The crying visitor is remembered fiction, not pictured.

entries.title: The quiet bit
entries.body: People come here for peace, then ask whether there's somewhere quieter. There is. They walked past it to get here.

entries.subject: river
entries.title: Unconstrained
entries.body: A man said he wished he could be as free as me. I am wedged between two mountains. I didn't like to interrupt.

image.sceneMatch: River runs through a mountain valley, directly supporting the joke's geographic constraint.

entries.subject: fern
entries.title: Primitive
entries.body: A person called me primitive. Then he tried three times to unfold his map.

image.sceneMatch: Finely divided green fern fronds support the visual contradiction of calling the organism primitive. Map and visitor are remembered fiction.

entries.subject: fern
entries.title: Winter advice
entries.body: The tree spent all summer telling me to reach for the light. Then it dropped every leaf it had. I asked whether it was still giving advice.

image.sceneMatch: An open green frond above fallen leaves supports evergreen persistence; no claim that the source photo documents winter or the particular tree.

entries.subject: fern
entries.title: Sideways rain
entries.body: I had planned to remain composed. Rain arrived sideways. For twenty minutes I was an extremely complicated mop.

image.sceneMatch: Intricate mature fern frond supplies the many fine surfaces in the mop comparison. Rain is a recalled event, not present in the image.

entries.subject: fern
entries.title: The hand
entries.body:
The hand lifted my oldest frond. The one with the brown edges. Of course.

There were perfectly good green ones on either side, but this was the one the person wanted. They held it against their palm and called someone over.

I prepared to be told what was wrong with me.

The second person took the hand instead. Turned it over. There was a little cut beside the thumb. The frond slipped free while they inspected that.

For several minutes the two of them forgot about me entirely. One fetched water. The other kept insisting it was nothing, while presenting the thumb from a slightly different angle.

I have brown edges, yes. But I have never required a second fern to admire them.

image.sceneMatch: A person's hand holds a frond with brown edges, supporting handling and the older leaf's appearance. Cut, second person and subsequent actions are fictional and not pictured.

entries.payoff: Fern's dread of criticism becomes an observation of human need for attention.

entries.subject: crocodile
entries.title: Free will
entries.body: He asked whether I believed in free will. I said yes. He asked me to move. I said no. He said I was a slave to comfort. I said yes.

image.sceneMatch: Mugger rests with its whole body supported across rocks; physical comfort and refusal to move are the scene. Conversational partner is not pictured.

entries.payoff: Declared free will immediately coexists with cheerful submission to comfort.

entries.subject: crocodile
entries.title: First journey
entries.body:
The first journey I remember was inside my mother's mouth.

There were teeth above us. Teeth beside us. My brother had a foot in my face and kept saying he couldn't see.

Mother carried us down to the water. The floor moved under our bellies. Every part of her that could have hurt us kept its distance.

I remember wanting the journey to last longer. I had only just hatched and already there was far too much outside.

Then cool water came in. We scrambled out. My brother immediately said he'd have preferred to walk.

He still tells people he was independent from birth. I was there. He complained about the view.

image.sceneMatch: Adult mugger with jaws open. This is explicitly Calder remembering maternal mouth transport, not a claim that the pictured animal is female or carrying hatchlings.

entries.subject: crocodile
entries.title: Listening
entries.body: The turtle asked if I was listening. I said yes. He asked what he'd just said. I told him he had just asked whether I was listening. He went away furious. I remain undefeated.

image.sceneMatch: Mugger lies with its eye closed, supporting deliberate inattention. Turtle conversation is remembered fiction, not pictured.

entries.subject: crocodile
entries.title: The long answer
entries.body: I went swimming to get away from an argument. Halfway across, I thought of the perfect answer. By the time I reached the other side, I couldn't remember what he'd said. I still have the answer. It's excellent. I'm saving it.

image.sceneMatch: Entire mugger swimming in open water, supporting physical withdrawal during the remembered argument.

entries.payoff: The perfect rebuttal survives after its reason has disappeared.
